candidates.title: Ner Tamid Lamp
candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Ner Tamid Lamp” by Virtual Museums of Małopolska (WirtualneMuzeaMalopolski), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: Full name: **Ner Tamid Lamp from the Great Synagogue in Oświęcim, Poland** Known as Ner Tamid (Hebrew: "eternal light"), the lamp symbolises the presence of divine light and as such should be kept aflame in a synagogue at all times, regardless whether the temple is open. This tradition is a reminder of the everlasting menorah in the Temple in Jerusalem (also known as The First Temple). The lamp on display was discovered, alongside other objects, during archeological excavations conducted in 2004 on the site once occupied by the [Great Synagogue in Oświęcim](https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/articles/673), before it was razed to the ground by the Nazis in November 1939. **For more images and further information, visit:** https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/2063 Inventory number: MŻ 9 Localisation of the physical object: Auschwitz Jewish Center, Oświęcim, Poland **Digitalisation: Regional Digitalisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland; “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” project**

candidates.title: Mezuzah from the house of Szymon Kluger
candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Mezuzah from the house of Szymon Kluger” by Virtual Museums of Małopolska (WirtualneMuzeaMalopolski), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: Full name: **Mezuzah from the house of Szymon Kluger in Oświęcim, Poland** Traditionally placed on the right-hand side doorpost of a Jewish house, a mezuzah is a piece of parchment encased in an ornamental box. It contains a hand-written excerpt from “Shema Yisrael” (Hebrew: Hear, O Israel), a Jewish prayer and a confession of belief in one transcendent God, taken from the Torah (Deuteronomy 6:4-9, 11:13-21). This unassuming plastic mezuzah is of no exceptional artistic value. Its importance is symbolic, as it is part of the collection of objects found in the house of Szymon Kluger (1925–2000), the last Jewish inhabitant of Oświęcim. **For more images and further information, visit:** https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/3005 Inventory number: MZ-348-O Localisation of the physical object: [Auschwitz Jewish Center](https://ajcf.pl/en/), Oświęcim, Poland **Digitalisation: Regional Digitalisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland; “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” project**

candidates.source_description: One of liturgical utensils of the Jewish faith is a vessel for scents called a spice tower (Hebrew: bassamim, psumin-byksy) used during Sabbath. The scent tower was probably created on the territory of Poland. It was made with the technique of intricate filigree typical of earlier scent towers coming from Polish goldsmith workshops. Unfortunately, it has no punch that would enable its precise identification. This spice tower represents the most common turret type. It has shape of a multi-storey synagogue situated on a square shape base set on four legs in the corners. candidates.source_description: Full name: **Bottle of kosher wine from the house of Szymon Kluger in Oświęcim, Poland** A bottle of kosher wine from the collection of objects found in the house of Szymon Kluger (1925–2000), the last Jewish resident of Oświęcim. In Judaism, for certain food products to be considered kosher (Hebrew: proper; fit for consumption), they have to be produced in accordance with strict Jewish dietary regulations known as “kashrut”. This applies to wine as well. The entire production process, starting from the crushing of the grapes and culminating in the bottling and sealing of the wine, ought to be supervised by a Shabbat-observant Jew. **For more images and further information, visit:** https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/2883 Inventory number: MZ-292-O Localisation of the physical object: [Auschwitz Jewish Center](https://ajcf.pl/en/), Oświęcim, Poland **Digitalisation: Regional Digitalisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland; “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” project**

candidates.title: Torah shield
candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Torah shield” by Virtual Museums of Małopolska (WirtualneMuzeaMalopolski), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: The shield (*tas*) is one of the elements of the ritual “outfit” of the synagogue Torah scroll (*klej kodesz*). Rectangular, closed with a trifoliate arch, with the figures of Moses (on the left) and Aaron (on the right), and the Tablets of Stone (in the middle), with the initial words of the Ten Commandments engraved in Hebrew. The figures of Moses and Aaron are flanked by spiral columns. On their plinths there are Hebrew inscriptions marking the date. In the three-leaf top, three openwork crowns with colourful glasses are attached. Between the crowns, on the plaque with floral motifs, there is an engraving of the Tetragrammaton. **For more images and further information, visit:** https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/552 Inventory number: MHK 282/VII Localisation of the physical object: Museum of Kraków, Poland **Digitalisation: Regional Digitalisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland; “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” project**

candidates.source_description: Octagonal-shaped baptismal font located to the rear of the Roman Catholic Church of the Nativity, in Ballynacarrigy, Co. Westmeath. In Christianity, the number eight represented rebirth and re-creation, a new beginning, and man's true "born again" event when he is resurrected from the dead into eternal life. The first historic reference is to Noah and his family as “eight persons were brought safely through the water” (1 Peter 3:20). Those eight persons experienced a true new beginning once the flood receded. It was eight days after the resurrection, when Thomas finally recognized the resurrection of Christ. In the Old Testament, God commanded the Israelites to circumcise newborn boys on the eighth day. It represented the start of a covenant with God, a covenant that was first sealed by Abraham. Jesus rose from the dead on Sunday. In the Hebrew calendar, Sunday is the first day of the week, also referred to as the eighth day.

Interestingly, the besamin box from Nowy Sącz is fish-shaped, whose head, connected to a trunk by a hinge, can be opened and tilted to the side. The fish trunk consists of five overlapping segments, each tapering towards the tail fin, each ending with semi-circular scales, each textured and covered in a network of furrows. The individual segments of the trunk are mutually conjoined in such a way that the body of the fish can be slightly bent. **For more images and further information, visit:** https://muzea.malopolska.pl/en/objects-list/696 Inventory number: MNS/3733/S Location of the physical object: Nowy Sącz District Museum, Poland **Digitalisation: Regional Digitalisation Lab, Małopolska Institute of Culture in Kraków, Poland; “Virtual Museums of Małopolska” Project**

candidates.title: Kidron Burial cave
candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Kidron Burial cave” by jerusalemheritage (jerusalemheritage), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: A Burial cave on the slope of the Kidron valley, east of the Temple Mount Kidron Valley is the modern name of the valley originating slightly northeast of the Old City of Jerusalem, which then separates the Temple Mount from the Mount of Olives, and ending at the Dead sea. The Kidron Valley Tombs are a set of burial monuments carved in the local limestone, in a section that faces the Temple Mount. Most famous are the “Tomb of Absalom” (in Hebrew Yad Avshalom), cave of Jehosaphat, and the Benei Hezir Tomb. Though none of the tombs bear an inscription with a date, they were probably created in the 1st century CE, by wealthy families of Jewish priests. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidron_Valley

candidates.title: Kidron Valley
candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Kidron Valley” by jerusalemheritage (jerusalemheritage), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: Kidron Valley is the modern name of the valley originating slightly northeast of the Old City of Jerusalem, which then separates the Temple Mount from the Mount of Olives, and ending at the Dead Sea. Beyond Jerusalem it continues in a general south-easterly direction through the Judean desert in the West Bank, reaching the Dead Sea near the settlement of Ovnat, and descending 4,000 feet (1,200 m) along its 20-mile (32 km) course. In ancient Hebrew sources, as well as in Arabic, different segments of the valley bear different names. Arabic names include Wadi el-Joz, 'Valley of the Walnut', but possibly a shortening of "Valley of Josaphat", for the upper segment, near the Temple Mount; and Wadi en-Nar, 'Fire Valley'. Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidron_Valley In the model we can see the section from Avshalom's tomb to Zacharia's tomb.

candidates.source_description: One room of Sennacherib’s (704–681 BC) palace at Nineveh was decorated with scenes of his dramatic destruction of Lachish, a Judean city that had rebelled against its Assyrian overlords. The siege of the city by an overwhelming military force resulted in its people being killed or led away as slaves. candidates.title: Treblinka 2013, Red Tile

candidates.attribution: 3D model “Treblinka 2013, Red Tile” by Centre-of-Archaeology (Centre-of-Archaeology), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: Treblinka, infamous in its role as one of the three Operation Reinhard death camps constructed by the Nazis to facilitate their genocide of European Jews, Poles and gypsies during the Holocaust, was actually two sites. These sites (Treblinka I (labour camp) and Treblinka II (extermination centre)) consisted of a series of buildings, including gas chambers and barracks. Tiles of this type (red ceramic with star motif) were a frequent find in Trench Treb04 (2013), located in the region where the gas chambers are believed to have been, suggesting that this tile originated from one of the chambers. candidates.source_description: # Jan Blažej Santini-Aichels Chapel of the Holy Sepulchre The Chapel of the Holy Sepulchre is a reminder of the place in Jerusalem where, according to tradition, Jesus Christ was laid after his crucifixion. The first temple was built over the Holy Sepulchre by Emperor Constantine in 326-335. Even then, the Holy Sepulchre itself was composed as a separate building in the middle of the temple. In the middle of the 16th century, the originally circular chapel acquired its characteristic appearance as a rectangular sanctuary with a horseshoe-shaped end, where the tomb of Christ was located. The surviving chapel of the [Holy Sepulchre at Zderaz](http://https://fel.cvut.cz/en/faculty/faculty-structure/chapel) (built around 1720) is described as a traditional copy of the Jerusalem building, although Santini's distinctive style was also applied to it, as shown by the unusual curved wall of the chapel's end and its typically Santinian morphology.

Built between 1926 and 1928 on the initiative of the “20 April” society and funded by benefactor Hadzhi Nencho Palaveev, it was designed by architect Panteley Tsvetkov. candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “Patrick Carpenter (1799-1818) Headstone No. 106” by Offaly Heritage (OffalyHeritage), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: 19th-century headstone (H 0.76m x Wth 0.45m x T 0.09m) in Old St. Brendan’s Graveyard (OF035-012002-), in the historic town of Birr (OF035-012----), marking the grave of Patrick Carpenter who died on the 19th of December in 1818 aged 19. Above the inscription there is an I H S Christogram with Latin Cross rising from the cross-bar of the H, flanked on either end by an encircled six-pointed rosette/star also known as a hexafoil, daisy-wheel, Star of David / of Bethlehem/of Creation. Luke 2:4 calls the Bethlehem where Christ was born “the City of David.” Jesus was born at the Tower of the Flock in Bethlehem Ephrata as well (Micah 4:8-5:2). One of the distinguishing features of Bethlehem Ephrata is the crocus flower that grows naturally there. This crocus flower is a small, purple, six-leafed flower with a yellow stigma. The six points are alleged to represent the six days of the Creation. In the 1821 Census of Birr the Carpenter family are recorded living at House No. 20 on Grave Yard Street.

candidates.source_description: Qumran (Hebrew: קומראן; Arabic: خربة قمران Khirbet Qumran) is an archaeological site in the West Bank managed by Israel's Qumran National Park. It is located on a dry marl plateau about 1.5 km (1 mi) from the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea, near the Israeli settlement and kibbutz of Kalya. The Hellenistic period settlement was constructed during the reign of Hasmonean leader John Hyrcanus (134–104 BCE) or somewhat later. Qumran was inhabited by a Jewish community of the Second Temple period, which most scholars identify with the mystic sect of the Essenes; however, other interpretations were also suggested. It was occupied most of the time until 68 CE and was destroyed by the Romans during the First Jewish-Roman War, possibly as late as 73 CE. It was later used by Jewish rebels during the Bar Kokhba Revolt.[6] Today, the Qumran site is best known as the settlement nearest to the Qumran Caves where the Dead Sea Scrolls were hidden, caves in the sheer desert cliffs and beneath, in the marl terrace.

candidates.source_description: **The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III** is a black limestone Assyrian sculpture with many scenes in bas-relief and inscriptions. It comes from Nimrud, in northern Iraq, and commemorates the deeds of King Shalmaneser III (858–824 BC). It is one of two complete Assyrian obelisks yet discovered, the other one being the much earlier White Obelisk of Ashurnasirpal I. This is historically significant because it is thought to display the earliest ancient depiction of a biblical figure – Jehu, King of Israel. Tribute offerings are shown being brought from identifiable regions and peoples. Wrapping around the pillar, the second row depicts the Israelites bringing homage to Shalmaneser, with Jehu depicted prostrate on the ground in front of the king of Assyria. It was erected as a public monument in 825 BC at a time of civil war, in the central square of Nimrud. It was discovered by archaeologist Sir Austen Henry Layard in 1846 and is now in the British Museum where I captured this 3D image from. –Nate Loper

A number of towns are situated there, most notably the city of Haifa, Israel's third largest city, located on the northern and western slopes. The range is a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Due to the lush vegetation on the sloped hillside, and many caves on the steeper side, Carmel became the haunt of criminals. In ancient Canaanite culture, high places were frequently considered to be sacred, and Mount Carmel appears to have been no exception. In mainstream Jewish, Christian, and Islamic thought, Elijah is associated with the mountain, and he is regarded as having sometimes resided on the mountain. The Bible's book of 1 Kings 18, records a showdown between Elijah and the prophets of Baal. In that account, the God of Elijah sends fire from heaven to consume a sacrifice of testing, proving which diety is the true and living one. The event takes place on this mountain. -Nate Loper

Some have theorized it may indeed have been King Tirhakah’s army who defeated the Assyrians rather than a supernatural angel, as the Hebrew word ‘malak’ translated as “angel” can also mean “messenger”, “servant”, or “emissary”. The same word is used many times elsewhere to refer to these latter titles given to people. Broken recumbent 19th-century headstone marking the graves of Mary Meara nee Humphrys (born c. 1778) who died in 1799 aged 21 and her husband Hugh Meara (born c. 1767) who died in 1801 aged 34. Above the inscription there is an I H S Christogram & Latin-Cross with expanded terminals rising from the crossbar of the H with sacred heart beneath contained within a sunburst flanked on either side by a soul-effigy with delicately carved flowers beneath. I N R I acronym across the centre of the cross. Acronym of the Latin phrase "Iesus Nazarenus, Rex Iudaeorum," which translates "Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews" in English. This inscription was placed on the cross of Jesus Christ, according to the Gospels. The inscription was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin on the cross, according to the Gospel of John.

candidates.source_description: 🔥 **Asmodeus: The Demon King of Desire** Asmodeus, known in Jewish lore as Ashmedai, is a powerful and malevolent spirit often associated with lust, chaos, and deception. He appears in the Book of Tobit, where he slays seven husbands of Sarah out of jealousy. In Talmudic tradition, he is portrayed as cunning and dangerous, yet oddly bound by rules and logic. Often depicted with monstrous features, horns, claws, and fiery eyes, Asmodeus is said to rule over legions of demons. Legends tell of King Solomon summoning and binding him to aid in building the Temple, showcasing his dual nature: destructive yet usable under divine command. Asmodeus embodies unchecked desire and the havoc it can wreak. He is a warning against indulgence without restraint, a figure both feared and studied in mystical traditions.

candidates.source_description: David Ben-Gurion born David Grün; 16 October 1886 – 1 December 1973) was the primary national founder of the State of Israel and the first Prime Minister of Israel. Adopting the name of Ben-Gurion in 1909, he rose to become the preeminent leader of the Jewish community in British-ruled Mandatory Palestine from 1935 until the establishment of the State of Israel in 1948, which he led until 1963. He retired from political life in 1970 and moved to Sde Boker, a kibbutz in the Negev desert, where he lived until his death. Posthumously, Ben-Gurion was named one of Time magazine's 100 Most Important People of the 20th century. The graves of David and his wif Paula Ben-Gurion overlook a breathtaking view of the Tsin canyon and the Avdat highlands in the heart of the Negev. candidates.source_description: 3D model of the allegorical figures of Ecclesia ("Church") and Synagoga ("Synagogue"). Dated to 1220 CE, these medieval sculptures originally adorned the south-eastern portal of the Strasbourg Cathedral. Today, these have been replaced by replicas and the originals (of which this 3D model is based from) is housed in the adjacent Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame. A common motif in medieval religious art, the figure of Ecclesia is depicted as triumphant with a crown, a chalice, and a staff surmounted by a cross. Meanwhile, Synagoga is depicted as blindfolded with a broken lance and the two tablets of the Law of Moses. 3D model generated using photogrammetry with a Nikon D3200 and processed in Agisoft Metashape. Makhtesh Ramon is the world's largest erosion crater, 40 km long and up to 10 km wide. candidates.subject: Jewish history
candidates.attribution: 3D model “O QUE ERA O ALTAR DO HOLOCAUSTO” by MARCIODIAS (MARCIODIAS), via Sketchfab, licensed CC Attribution.
candidates.source_description: O QUE REPRESENTAVA O ALTAR DO HOLOCAUSTO O altar do holocausto representava o “calvário”, o caminho da salvação para o pecador. No altar do holocausto o pecador tinha seus pecados expiados. Aqui é uma figura exata de Cristo. O Cordeiro de Deus fez-se de oferta para expiar todo o pecado da humanidade. Ele é “o Cordeiro de Deus, que tira o pecado do mundo” (Jo 1.29). Assim, nosso Senhor suportou, em nosso lugar, o juízo de Deus sobre o pecado, fazendo-se pecado por nós (Is 53.4,10; Zc 13.7; Mt 26.39; 1 Tm 2.5,6). PARA QUE SERVIA O ALTAR Vamos começar com o primeiro tópico – Para que servia o altar do holocausto? O altar do holocausto servia para sacrificar ofertas para Deus. Algumas ofertas eram pelos seus próprios pecados e outras pelos pecados do povo. O propósito do holocausto era que por meio dele, as pessoas fossem aceitas e perdoadas diante de Deus (Levítico 1:4). Para o holocausto, um animal macho era sacrificado: um carneiro, um bode, um boi ou uma rola (ou um pombinho) (Levítico 1:13-17).

candidates.source_description: The Lachish relief is found in gallery 10b of the British Museum, and they were originally discovered in the South West palace of [Nineveh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineveh). This set of gypsum wall panels depicts the Assyrian army laying siege to the town of [Lachish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Lachish) (modern-day Tell ed-Duweir, Israel), found about 40 kilometres SW from Jerusalem (in 701 BC). In this depiction, we can see soldiers storming the town walls, and prisoners taken can be seen being expelled into exile, whilst others are flayed. The relief was created for the walls of the great palace of the Assyrian king, Sennacherib, in Nineveh. This set of panels provides propaganda to demonstrate why rebellion against the King was futile. For more information see [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lachish_reliefs). candidates.source_description: Neskoro barokový ústredný kamenný kríž sa nachádza na cintoríne v obci Križovany nad Dudváhom, okres Trnava, Trnavský kraj. Situovaný je uprostred cintorína. Predmetný kríž je najstaršou sakrálnou pamiatkou v areáli cintorína. Kríž sa skladá z troch častí: krucifix, stĺp a dvojdielný podstavec. Vyrobený je z neznámeho druhu kameňa. V hornej časti sa nachádza plastický korpus Ukrižovaného Krista na kríži a nad ním latinský nápis v tvare listu s písmenami I(esus) N(azarenus) R(ex) I(udaeorum) (Ježiš Nazaretský, Kráľ Židovský). V strednej časti sa nachádza plastická figúra Sedembolestnej Panny Márie, ktorá je umiestnená na podstavci. Na čelnej strane podstavca sa nachádza datovanie v latinčine Anno 1782 (rok 1782), ktoré poukazuje na vznik a osadenie tejto sakrálne pamiatky. Na zadnej strane podstavca sa nachádza pamätná tabuľa v slovenčine s menami kňazov, ktorí pôsobili vo farnosti Križovany nad Dudváhom a sú pochovaní na miestnom cintoríne. Menovite Ján Jozef Hošek, Juraj Kováč, Matej Čubaj a Ján Rohovský.

candidates.title: WMID-AFEBBB Medieval cruciform pendant

candidates.source_description: A complete, cast silver, cruciform pendant dating from the medieval period, with the inscription AGLA. The pendant has been cast as one piece. It consists of a circular lobe from which four arms project out. Three of these arms are topped by globular knobs, roughly 5mm wide. The fourth arm at the top of the pendant is shorter, with another smaller globular knob 4.1mm wide at its end and a large circular loop, 6.7mm in diameter continuing from the knob. The central lobe has engraved decoration on both faces, consisting of a circular border with large, clear, capital letters within. On the front the letters read AG, and on the reverse they read LA, with large flat serifs. AGLA was a popular charm used in the medieval period to fend off fever and possibly also the Black Death. The letters are an abbreviation of a Hebrew saying, "Ata gibor le'olam Adonai" (You are mighty forever, O Lord). It has been recorded on finger-rings as well as pendants.
